the spin polarization of the tunnel barrier is the most important parameter to determine the performance of a magnetic tunnel transistor.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new materials for spintronic devices.
the spin-dependent electron tunneling at interfaces between ferromagnetic metals and insulators.
the spin transport and spin manipulation in semiconductors, with a focus on the spin injection from ferromagnetic metals and the spin transport in semiconducting nanostructures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SiO2 is not a suitable tunnel barrier material for spin injection in Si.
the spin polarization of a Ni80Fe2O/SiO2 junction is 27% and that the spin polarization is not significantly affected by the SiO2 interfacial layer.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed the first magnetic tunnel transistor, which is a device for the electrical detection of spin polarization in ferromagnet/oxide interfaces.
we have demonstrated the possibility to fabricate a magnetic tunnel transistor with an emitter of Ni80Fe 20/SiO 2.
the spin polarization of the tunnel junctions can be increased with the use of the SiO2 layer as the tunnel barrier.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spin polarization of the emitter is a key parameter in the design of magnetic tunnel transistors.
SiO2 is a promising candidate for spin injection into semiconductors, and that the tunnel spin polarization of SiO2 can even be higher than for Al2O3.
